title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ(松下裕研究室)
subtitle: Design Project III(Matsushita Yutaka)
educationalGoal: This course integrates what has been learned so far. The purpose of this course is to provide students with opportunities to discover problems (e.g., usability, response time) that are involved in the use of digital contents (videos and websites) and to propose solutions. In order to create digital contents useful for people and society, students will not only create digital contents based on the knowledge they have learned so far but will also assess the physiological properties and emotional states of people using the contents.
advice: Our laboratory aims to teach mastery of the techniques used to effectively edit scenes of videos and to design attractive websites. In order to create digital contents that people can easily use and enjoy, the assessment of their physiological properties and emotional states is just as important as the technique used to create the contents. Therefore, aiming to develop a human sensory measurement technology based on data analysis methods and psychological knowledge, students will use their acquired knowledge to create novel digital contents. Learning Tips: Students of this course are expected to take a full year to solve the problems that they have raised. To ensure this work progresses smoothly, it is important that their research themes be set properly. Indeed, if students set a research theme to which they are strongly committed, they will be able to devote their energies to acquiring necessary knowledge and deriving new ideas, even when they experience difficulties. Additionally, although some may feel that bibliographical search and information gathering process are redundant when determining themes, students should be aware that they are extremely helpful for solving related problems.
requiredKnowledge: Students are required to have completed all the prerequisite subjects of the department. Students must be able to generalize what they have learned from the first to third year. Students are expected to have mastered some of the techniques used for creating digital contents or a technique of programming.

activityGoals.body: Be able to demonstrate basic ability as a creative engineer by setting a problem and providing its solution.
Be able to explain contents related to your specialized field.
Be able to deepen insights into "engineer ethics."
Be able apply specialized expertise to the project theme.
Be able to conduct CDIO-based research and development on the set project theme.

achievementLevels.ideal: Satisfy an achievement rate of more than 90% for all action goals.
achievementLevels.standard: Satisfy an achievement rate between 60% and 80% for all action goals.

lessons.content: By reading papers related to their set research theme, each student determines digital content to be created, clarifies the accompanying problems, and then imagines solutions. Before the summer vacation, each student will create a prototype of their content and identify problems. If necessary, students will be expected to acquire any missing skills during their summer vacation.
lessons.operation: Each student reads papers and gives a presentation. This is done in the form of a seminar, and all participants will discuss and comprehend the contents.
lessons.assignments: Students study their specialized fields and investigate their project theme for about nine hours each week.

lessons.content: In the first half, a preliminary experiment is conducted for the evaluation of a digital content. Students will recreate the content if necessary. In the second half, a full-scale experiment is conducted, after which students analyze results, consider them, and derive conclusions related to the problem. Ultimately, each student integrates their research results to create clear documents.
lessons.operation: Each student reports their progress and analysis results. If necessary, the seminar is conducted on analysis methods. Guidance is provided for creating project reports and presentations.
lessons.assignments: Students study analysis methods and endeavor to complete their research project for about nine hours each week.
